## Purpose

**Robust Statistical Methods for Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Test Accuracy** is the long-term scope of this package.
The initial version implements Project I distributional diagnostics only.


The bivariate GLMM for diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis commonly assumes
that study-specific sensitivity and specificity effects follow a bivariate
normal distribution. Directly applying the classical HZ test to empirical
Bayes estimates can be affected by unequal study precision and shrinkage.

`dtaIPDMA` implements a weighted statistic that combines:

1. empirical Bayes study effects from the fitted bivariate GLMM;
2. the fitted between-study covariance matrix; and
3. study-specific within-study variances derived from each 2-by-2 table.

Because the null distribution of the weighted statistic is not available in
closed form, inference uses a parametric bootstrap.

## Input data

```{r}
library(dtaIPDMA)
dat <- scoff
head(dat)
```

The input must contain raw integer counts. Continuity correction is applied
internally only when calculating within-study variances.

## Run both tests

```{r}
tests <- dta_hz_test(dat, B = 499, nAGQ = 7, seed = 2026)
tests$summary
```

For a preliminary code check, a small `B` may be used. Final analyses should
use enough bootstrap samples to achieve suitable Monte Carlo precision.

## Inspect the weighted test

```{r}
print(tests$weighted)
summary(tests$weighted)
plot_dta_effects(tests$weighted, type = "density", weighted = TRUE)
plot_dta_effects(tests$weighted, type = "qq", weighted = TRUE)
```

The reported `B_effective` is the number of bootstrap datasets for which the
GLMM and weighted statistic were successfully obtained.

## Parallel bootstrap

On a laptop with eight logical processors, six workers are a sensible choice:

```{r}
tests <- dta_hz_test(
  dat, B = 499, nAGQ = 5, seed = 2026,
  parallel = TRUE, n_cores = 6
)
```

## Individual participant data and covariates

For IPD, provide the disease status and index-test result as numeric `0/1`
variables. Covariates are centred within study before fitting the GLMM.

```{r}
ipd_tests <- ipd_hz_test(
  data = ipd_data,
  study_id = "study_id",
  disease = "disease",
  test = "test_result",
  covariates = c("age", "sex"),
  B = 499, nAGQ = 7, parallel = TRUE, n_cores = 6, seed = 2026
)
```
